nodes.body:

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Fedora 43

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

never worked

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Desktops Affected

KDE Plasma 6.3+ OR labwc 0.90+ (they both have toplevel icon protocol for Wayland)

### Expected Behavior

I expected both cases in "Additional Information" section to both display the icon

### Actual Behavior

this does not work to display the icon

```js
const win = new BaseWindow({
  width: 800,
  height: 600,
  icon: myIcon,
})
```

---

this does work to display the icon, but both cases should work

```js
const win = new BaseWindow({
  width: 800,
  height: 600,
})

win.setIcon(myIcon)
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Try the following code with `// icon: myIcon,` or `// win.setIcon(myIcon)` uncommented

```js
const { app, BaseWindow } = require('electron')

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  const myIcon =  'icon.png'

  const win = new BaseWindow({
    width: 800,
    height: 600,
    // icon: myIcon,
  })

  // win.setIcon(myIcon)
})
```

nodes.body:

### Electron Version

39.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Sequoia 15.7.2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

The Dictionary Lookup should either work within the Kiosk context without breaking the window state, or be suppressed entirely to maintain Kiosk integrity.

### Actual Behavior

The Kiosk mode is violated (e.g., window switches to dictionary, dock appears, menu bar appers, app loses focus and able to switch processes and others) when the definition popover appears.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/jayagrawal254/4e7e89451ac76249d44c457ac76fbd22

### Additional Information

### Reproduction Steps:

1. Create an Electron window with **kiosk: true**
2. Run the application on **macOS**.
3. Highlight text or hover over a word.
4. Trigger the "**Look up**" feature (Through keyboard)
- _System Preferences -> Keyboard -> Services -> Look Up in Dictionary_
5. Observe: The Kiosk window loses focus/state or the OS UI interferes, violating Kiosk rules.

Unknown/Cant Check

### Expected Behavior

```ts
'audioTracks' in HTMLVideoElement.prototype
```
Should return true when

```ts
  new BrowserWindow({
    webPreferences: {
      enableBlinkFeatures: 'AudioVideoTracks'
    }
  })
```

Is used

> [!NOTE]
> This is not limited to `audioTracks`. It happens with other features, too.

### Actual Behavior

no audio tracks support, `'enable-experimental-web-platform-features'` works but is problematic as it enables a lot of other bad things

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/ThaUnknown/c2a77abe289f98b23d7cae4f92ee204f

### Additional Information

I have NO clue how to properly create a test case for this.

This ONLY happens if the initial load of the browserview is served from a service worker cache, if it's loaded directly over network this bug doesnt occur. Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy/Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy headers/crossOriginIsolation is required for this bug to occur.

nodes.title: Support `resign-key` and `become-key` events on `BrowserWindow` (macOS)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, Electron’s `BrowserWindow` exposes `focus` and `blur` events, but it does not expose the native macOS `NSWindow` events for `windowDidBecomeKey` and `windowDidResignKey`.

While `focus` and `blur` often correlate with key status, they are not semantically identical, especially when building floating panels, overlays, or "spotlight-like" interfaces (`NSPanel`).

### Proposed Solution

Expose the native [`windowDidBecomeKey`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindowdelegate/windowdidbecomekey(_:)) and [`windowDidResignKey`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindowdelegate/windowdidresignkey(_:)) events as `become-key` and `resign-key` (or similar) on the `BrowserWindow` instance. I noticed that `BrowserWindow::OnWindowIsKeyChanged(bool is_key)` already exists in `electron_api_browser_window.cc` ([source link](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/809ab09b6f5ede0a9f9b0fcc0e9c33ff971277f2/shell/browser/api/electron_api_browser_window.cc#L188)), but it does not appear to be mapped to a public-facing event that consumers can listen to.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Native Modules:** I'm currently using a native module to access `NSWindowDelegate` methods directly.
- **Using `blur` event:** It does not map 1:1 with `resignKey` behavior in multi-window setups, when i don't want to capture focus.

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Forced termination (SIGKILL) of multiple Electron apps on macOS 26.2 Tahoe without crash reports
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

32.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

26.2

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

### Summary

### Actual Behavior

### Summary
On macOS 26.2 Tahoe (latest official release), multiple Electron-based applications are being **force-terminated by the system (SIGKILL)** without generating crash reports. These terminations happen even with the latest versions of the applications and with up-to-date macOS.

This behaviour goes beyond UI lag/stutter described in other issues (e.g., #48311). In my case, apps such as VS Code, Slack, Chrome, and other Electron apps are killed by the OS abruptly without crash logs, often correlated with sustained WindowServer activity.

I have collected sysdiagnose output showing high WindowServer involvement shortly before the terminations. This appears to be a system resource / compositor rendering interaction issue rather than an app-specific crash.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Boot macOS 26.2 Tahoe on Apple Silicon (M4/Mx).
2. Open multiple Electron-based applications (VS Code, Slack, Chrome, etc.).
3. Work normally (code editing, multiple windows, no special operations).
4. After some time, one or more apps are killed by the OS without warnings or crash reports.

### Expected Behavior
Electron apps should not be abruptly terminated by the OS without crash reports. Users should be able to work without unexpected force quits.

### Actual Behavior
Apps are abruptly terminated (SIGKILL) by the system. No crash report is generated in Console for these terminations.

### Context
Related Electron compatibility discussions include performance and rendering issues on macOS 26 (e.g., #48311), but this report reflects **forced termination behaviour**, which has not been documented in existing open issues:

• Strange global lag / WindowServer issues — https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48311 :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}  
• VS Code GPU/WindowServer behaviour discussions — https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/267022 :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

### Additional Files / Logs

nodes.title: Allow Renderer's DNS cache cleanup using Session#clearHostResolverCache()
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Right now `Session#clearHostResolverCache()` affects only the next calls of `Session#resolveHost()` which doesn't affect Renderer processes even if the same `Session` object was passed to `BrowserWindow`. This results in absolute lack of control over Renderer's DNS cache.

### Proposed Solution

Make `Session#clearHostResolverCache()` clear Renderer's DNS cache

### Alternatives Considered

The only alternative for the proposed solution is providing an another API for Renderer's DNS cache control which is weird since `Session` is the API designed to control the Chromium's network capabilities

### Additional Information

nodes.title: Enhance Electron spawn lifecycle handling for better robustness
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

 The current Node.js script that spawns and manages the Electron process works correctly, but it can be improved for robustness, safety, and maintainability.
Some edge cases (like spawn failure or multiple event listeners) are not fully handled.

### Proposed Solution

Use child.once() instead of child.on() for lifecycle events

Handle the exit event in addition to close

Add a listener for the error event on the spawned process

Refactor signal handling to avoid repetition

### Alternatives Considered

Prevents accidental multiple event triggers

Avoids silent crashes if Electron fails to start

Improves code readability and intent

Makes the process lifecycle handling more production-safe

### Additional Information

The child process lifecycle should be handled safely and deterministically

Spawn failures should be caught and reported clearly

Event listeners should be registered only once

Signal handling should be concise and easier to extend

Ubuntu

Ubuntu 25.10 / Linux 6.17.0-8-generic #8-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Nov 14 21:44:46 UTC 2025 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When using OSR with `useSharedTexture: true`, a paint event should be fired with a properly populated texture.

### Actual Behavior

The following error is output, and the paint event does not fire:

```
[93649:1220/233451.235840:ERROR:gpu/command_buffer/service/shared_image/shared_image_representation.cc:408] Unable to initialize SkSurface
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

According to this post by @reitowo:
[https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/46811#issuecomment-2859463799](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/46811#issuecomment-2859463799)

it appears that the issue does not occur on Linux environments equipped with AMD GPUs. Since AMD-based environments have had Wayland as the default for quite some time, it is assumed that this setup is also running on Wayland.

If that is the case, the only plausible difference between that environment and mine is the GPU itself. Therefore, it seems reasonable to conclude that OSR is not supported on NVIDIA + Linux + Wayland environments. There are no display issues or errors when using non-OSR windows or when rendering in Chrome/Chromium.

For reference, I have attached the `about://gpu` report. The flags `enable-unsafe-webgpu` and `ignore-gpu-blocklist` are enabled, but disabling them does not change the behavior.

### Electron Version

38.2.0 ~ 39.2.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 25.10, also heard of it happening on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

38.1.2

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

App to launch

### Actual Behavior

Segfault: `node_modules/electron/dist/electron exited with signal SIGSEGV`
(unless the `BrowserWindow` has `frame: false`, then is works as expected for some reason)

### Testcase Gist URL

unable

### Additional Information

Couldn't get Fiddle to run, so here's the code:
### `package.json`:
```json
{
  "name": "electron-test",
  "main": "main.js",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "electron ."
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "electron": ">=38.2.0"
  }
}
```

### `main.js`:
```js
const {app, BrowserWindow} = require("electron")

function createWindow() {
	const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
		// frame: false // Uncomment to stop segfault from occurring
	})

	 // Not reached
	console.log("No segfault!")
}

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  createWindow()
})
```

Someone [on reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/electronjs/comments/1oc7qvi/crash_on_new_browserwindow/) identified that `frame: false` stops the segfault, I would never have figured that out myself

Hi Electron team and maintainers 👋

### Proposed Solution

I'm the author of UpgradeLink, an open-source, zero-modification-integration auto-upgrade tool specifically designed for Electron applications. I’m opening this issue to suggest adding UpgradeLink to the Electron official documentation’s recommended tools for app upgrades.

UpgradeLink is completely open-source and free to use. The detailed Electron integration documentation and usage guide can be found here:   https://github.com/toolsetlink/upgradelink/blob/main/README_en.md

**Why it would be valuable for Electron developers**

Reduces the learning curve for new Electron developers who want to implement auto-upgrades without diving deep into Electron’s complex updater configurations.

Fills the gap of lightweight, out-of-the-box upgrade tooling that the current outdated docs lack.
Saves development resources for teams of all sizes (indie developers, startups, enterprises) building Electron apps, allowing them to focus on core functionality instead of upgrade logic.

If the team finds this tool useful, I would be honored to see it listed in the Electron docs’ recommended tools section. Contributions, feedback, and collaboration are always welcome!

Thank you for your hard work on maintaining Electron! 🚀
